page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The instance features 64 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage spread across four local drives, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features an 80 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-standard-16-lssd demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, achieving a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score and strong results in large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth. Compute performance is characterized by strong single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores, alongside strong throughput in text processing, image processing, and single-threaded gzip compression. Database operations and static web serving throughput also register in the strong tier, while multi-core stress-ng and Redis SET operations perform within the average range.

Given its dedicated ARMv8 cores, high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and strong memory bandwidth, this instance is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. The lack of hyperthreading and the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio make it a resource-dense option for general-purpose workloads requiring high local I/O performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM architecture delivers competitive compute density and memory performance relative to traditional x86 alternatives, though workloads requiring AVX or AMX instruction sets are unsupported.
